runs.text: A program reads 5 numbers and then a searched number, and shows the position of the first appearance of the searched number, or -1 if it is not there. Write between 3 and 4 test cases so that any wrong version fails at least one.

hints.text: Imagine how a search can go wrong: where it starts, when it stops, what it answers if it finds nothing.
Each case has to test one of those decisions.
You need a repeated searched number, one in the first position and one that is not there.
With repeats (3, 7, 9, 7, 1 and 7 → 1), in position 0 (7, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 → 0) and absent (→ -1). Close with the variant.

runs.text: Why does the visible case uncover none of the three wrong versions? (15 appears once, it is not in position 0 and it is there.)
Wrong versions: returns the last appearance, starts searching at position 1 and answers 0 when it finds nothing. Each of the three cases of the solution uncovers one.
